## What I did today

Today we learn about **environments** and why the same code can give different
results on two different computers.

The environment we looked at is called
**Pixi**.

## Why do we use environments?

An environment keeps each project separate. 
It also means someone else can rebuild the exact same setup on their own
computer. 

## Installing Pixi

One line in the terminal:

```bash
wget -qO- https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
```

## Starting a project

Make a new environment for the project:

```bash
pixi init lina_pixi_training -c conda-forge -c bioconda
```

The `-c` parts say where to download software from. 

This creates two files:

- **`pixi.toml`** — the short, readable one. It lists the project name and the
  tools I asked for. This is the file I actually edit.
- **`pixi.lock`** — the long, automatic one. It records the exact versions and
  where they came from. I never edit this by hand, but it is the file that
  makes the setup truly reproducible.
